implementations.name: AccountEraseDialog
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-account/danger/AccountEraseDialog — the WEB account-erasure dialog (CR-002 / U4b).

A controlled `Dialog` built on `@radix-ui/react-dialog` — Radix owns focus-trapping, Escape-to-dismiss,
backdrop-click dismiss, and the `role="dialog"` + `aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby` wiring from its
`Title`/`Description` parts, so this leaf only supplies the Commise visual language, the donate election,
and the phrase gate. `onOpenChange(false)` (Escape + backdrop) maps onto the same `onCancel` the explicit
Cancel button uses — one exit path, not two.

The confirm action is enabled ONLY when {@link confirmsErasurePhrase} accepts the typed phrase and no
submit is in flight — the SAME predicate the native leaf uses, so the two platforms gate identically and
neither can enable a confirmation the server would `400`.

The frame and type roles are the Close dialog's (`@commise/ui` `ConfirmDialog`): a `rounded-lg` `paper-overlay`
panel, a `section-title` title, a `body` / `inkMuted` description, the design-system `Input` and buttons. The
warning is not painted red end to end; a `dangerText` glyph stands beside it, and its words already say
"permanently" and "cannot be undone", so colour is never the only cue (`buildSpec.md` §10). It stays a Radix
`Dialog`, not the `AlertDialog` under `ConfirmDialog`, because it holds a form (the donate election and the phrase).

implementations.name: AccountEraseDialog
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-account/danger/AccountEraseDialog.native — the NATIVE account-erasure dialog
(CR-002 / U4b). The React Native leaf of `AccountEraseDialog` — the
SAME controlled, presentational contract, phrase gate, and donate election as the web leaf, so the two
platforms can never drift on behaviour or on which inputs enable the destructive confirm.

Renders nothing while `open` is false: the frame returns early rather than toggling `Modal`'s `visible`, because
under `react-native-web` a `Modal` keeps its portal content mounted across a `visible` toggle.

The window, the scrim, the safe area, the keyboard and the card are the design system's `DialogFrame`
(`docs/design/compactHeightLayout.md` §9): sideways, the keyboard used to cover the phrase field and both actions,
with nothing to move them. Taps persist through the keyboard, so the first tap on Erase presses it.

implementations.name: DisplayNameSheet
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-account/profile/DisplayNameSheet — the display-name sheet (web): "What should we call
you?", one field and Save (`buildSpec.md` §9.1).

The name can show publicly as an author handle, so this sheet is the only place the app asks for it and it saves
only when Save is pressed (or Enter in the field) — never on close and never from the prefill alone. Controlled and
stateless: the page owns the draft, the gate (`canSaveDisplayName`) and the write.

The field stops at its limit (a hard `maxLength`: the name is a public handle), so from 80 % of it a counter says how
close the cook is (W-26). The counter is NOT a live region (it would speak on every key); a separate polite one says
once that the limit is reached.

implementations.name: LabelValuePair
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-account/profile/LabelValuePair — a label with its value (web): beside it, the value at the
end of the line, or under it at the start, 4 px below, when the group's column (its `rows` container, `ProfileGroup`)
has less than 17.5 rem of room (designer rulings 2026-11-01, `nativeBoards/designAnswers.md`). 17.5 rem is native's
280 at the default text size, and a rem follows the browser's text size. `ProfileFactRow` and `ProfileRow` draw their
label and value through it. A pair with no `rows` container above it never stacks.

The label is the caller's own element and a direct flex child, so its minimum width is its longest word and it never
breaks inside one. The value wraps anywhere and never truncates. Each variant is written out whole, because Tailwind
generates only the class names it finds.

Presentational: props → JSX.

implementations.name: LabelValuePair
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-account/profile/LabelValuePair — a label with its value (native): beside it, the value at the
END of the line, or under it at the start when the column has too little room for the text size (designer rulings
2026-11-01, `nativeBoards/designAnswers.md`). `ProfileFactRow` and `ProfileRow` draw their label and value through it.

The room is `labelValueStacksAt(contentWidthOf(width), cappedFontScale(fontScale))`, read from the window here and
nowhere else in the Profile rows: the content width is the house's (`contentWidthOf`, as the recipe page and the list
results read it), and the scale is the one the text is drawn at (`cappedFontScale`).

Beside the value the label does not shrink, so it never breaks inside a word, and the value takes what is left and
wraps; it never truncates. Stacked, the two sit `$1` apart, one group. React Native's `textAlign: 'right'` is the
line's end: React Native 0.86 swaps 'right' and 'left' when the text's layout direction is right to left (iOS
`RCTAttributedTextUtils.mm`, Android `TextLayoutManager.getTextAlignment`), so 'left' is the start by the same swap.

Presentational: props → JSX, with the window's size read as the design system's `Text` reads it.

implementations.name: ProfileRow
implementations.moduleDoc:
@commise/features-account/profile/ProfileRow — a pressable Profile row (web): 56 px, the label, its value,
an optional hint, and a chevron when it opens something (`buildSpec.md` §9.1). A row with a value draws the label and
the value as a `LabelValuePair`: the value wraps and never truncates, and it stacks under the label when the group's
column has too little room (designer ruling 2026-11-01, `nativeBoards/designAnswers.md`). The chevron stays at the
row's end either way.

One control: the whole row is the button (or the link, when it has a destination), and its hint is inside it, so the
consequence of Close account is read with the name. The danger tone changes the TEXT colour only. Sign out is `ink`:
it is not destructive. While busy the row stays focusable and cancels the press (`aria-busy`), the same rule as the
design-system `Button` (SC 2.4.3). An `inert` row (its action is done) does the same without `aria-busy`: nothing is
in flight, so it announces disabled and ignores the press, and is not dimmed.

props.name: busy
props.description: The row is mid-action: it cannot be pressed again and says so to assistive tech.

props.name: chevron
props.description: Whether a chevron says the row opens something.

props.name: focusSignal
props.description:
Native only: a count the host advances when the sheet this row opened closes. A change takes the screen-reader
cursor back to the row (WCAG 2.4.3; `buildSpec.md` §10 "Dialogs and sheets"), because React Native cannot say
where the cursor was. The first value moves nothing. Web ignores it: Radix returns focus to the opener itself.

props.name: hint
props.description: A caption under the label (the danger rows' consequence).

props.name: href
props.description: Web only: where a link row goes, so a modified click still works. Native ignores it.

props.name: inert
props.description:
The row's action is DONE and cannot run again ("Account closed"). Presses are ignored and it reads as disabled,
but it is not `busy` (nothing is in flight), not dimmed (it is a fact, not an unavailable control), and on web it
stays focusable so focus is never dropped (SC 2.4.3). `busy` and `inert` never hold together.

props.name: tone
props.description: `ink` for ordinary rows. `danger` for the danger zone's text.

props.name: value
props.description: The current value. It wraps and never truncates, and stacks under the label when the row has little room.

erasure that was accepted but whose exit failed.
